anomalies.observed: On the second sheet the LM1117-5.0 regulator U4 has BOTH its input pin (2, VI) and its output pin (3, VO) tied to the global net +5V (two separate '+5V' arrows above pins 2 and 3). The net 'VCC' that is used on the first sheet (C3 decoupling, R4 pull-up, Q2 source, JP2 pin 2) is therefore never driven by the regulator.
anomalies.expected: A linear regulator's input and output must be two different nets: VI should be the raw +5V supply and VO should feed the regulated VCC rail (the rail that C3, R4 and the high-side P-FET Q2 are connected to). As drawn, VI and VO are shorted together and the VCC rail is left floating.

evidence.quote: U4 LM1117-5.0: pin 2 VI -> +5V, pin 3 VO -> +5V, pin 1 GND (sheet /, second page, top-left)
VCC net on first page carries C3 100nF, R4 10K pull-up and Q2 source, with no connection to U4 output (sheet /, first page, row A/B)

anomalies.impact: The regulator is bypassed (input shorted to output) and the VCC rail has no source, so the fan high-side driver Q2, its gate pull-up R6, and the VCC pull-up R4 are all left floating; the fan output stage will not power up as intended.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the LM1117-5.0 (U4) with its input (pin 2) and output (pin 3) both connected to the +5V net, shorting the regulator and leaving the separate VCC rail (used by C3, R4 and the P-FET Q2) undriven; this is the most likely deviation from the intended ATtiny fan-controller design.
